g.text: ISLANDS • CITIES • ECONOMY • PEOPLE • PLACES TO VISIT
Japan is an island nation in East Asia, stretching
3,000 km along the Pacific Ring of Fire. Its four
main islands — Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and
Shikoku — plus 14,000 smaller isles host 124 million
people, with 92% living in densely built coastal plains.
Known for blending ancient tradition with cutting-
edge technology, Japan pairs Shinto shrines and
Zen gardens with bullet trains, robotics and a
global cultural engine from woodblock prints to anime.
Capital Tokyo anchors the world's largest metro area
(37M). Yokohama, Osaka and Nagoya form the

text.tspan: Despite limited natural resources and frequent seismic activity, Japan built one of the world's most resilient societies
, emphasizing precision, craftsmanship and collective harmony. From Edo-period woodblock prints to contemporary design and cuisine
, its influence extends far beyond its archipelago — shaping global aesthetics while maintaining deep respect for seasonality, ritual and nature.

g.text: Nominal GDP trajectory reflects yen fluctuations
as much as real growth. After peaking near $5.12T
in 2019, the yen's depreciation against the dollar
pushed dollar-denominated GDP down to $4.03T in
2024, even as domestic output remained stable.
automotive exports remain core pillars. Japan is
the world's 4th largest economy and top creditor
